market_snapshot.breadth_notes: Prior session (Tue Oct 13): S&P 500 7,805 (-0.02%), Dow 51,670 (-0.35%), Nasdaq 27,204 (-0.15%), Russell 2000 -0.4%; PHLX Semiconductor Index -2.7%, fifth straight down session and down ~5% in October. Split tape: megacaps held up (META +2.6%, NVDA +0.9%, MSFT +0.4%, AMD +1.9%) while memory/equipment sold off (MU -3.6%, AMAT -6.6%) and big banks faded (Citi -5.6%, WFC -3.1%, JPM -0.9% rare profit miss). Advance/decline and volume-vs-20d not shown on sourced pages. Overnight Asia: KOSPI +1.8% recovering, Samsung and SK Hynix each +2%+; Nikkei -0.05%.
market_snapshot.notes: Premarket Wed Oct 14, ~4 AM PT (2.5h before the 6:30 AM PT open). Futures edging up into the September CPI print (5:30 AM PT) and a second wave of bank earnings before the open (BAC, MS, BLK, STT). ASML's Q3 print brought the first hard demand evidence against the memory rout. Energy elevated: Brent ~$105.50-106.60 amid Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and IEA demand forecast.

headlines.headline: Futures edging higher ahead of September CPI: Dow e-minis +0.45%, S&P 500 e-minis +0.21%, Nasdaq 100 e-minis roughly flat at -0.03% (per Reuters ~5:41 AM ET).
headlines.why_it_matters: A calm, bid tape into the 8:30 AM ET print — September CPI is the last inflation read before the Oct 27-28 FOMC, and the market is pricing a hot-vs-hold debate rather than a directional bet yet.

headlines.headline: September CPI lands today 8:30 AM ET (5:30 AM PT): consensus 3.6% y/y headline (from 3.4%), +0.6% m/m, core +0.2% m/m and 2.5% y/y. FedWatch: ~22% chance of an October hike, ~89% for a December hike.
headlines.why_it_matters: The core monthly print is the decider — ~0.2% keeps the Fed on hold, ~0.3% revives October hike bets and hits both bonds and stocks; every other headline today trades downstream of this number.

headlines.headline: 10Y at 5.20% (-2bp overnight, -3bp vs Tuesday's brief); NY Fed's Williams: one more hike this year may be appropriate, no hikes in 2027. Boston Fed's Collins: not rethinking the 2% target. JPMorgan's Dimon warned financial pressure could intensify if rates rise another point.
headlines.why_it_matters: Fedspeak is anchoring the terminal path (one more, then done) while bonds rally into CPI — a soft core print would validate the whole move, a hot one reprices it instantly.

headlines.headline: ASML Q3: record revenue EUR11.66B (a touch below the EUR11.71B Visible Alpha consensus), net profit EUR4.96B beating expectations, gross margin 57.5%. Raised FY26 sales guidance to EUR44-45B from EUR43-45B — third raise this year — and guided Q4 sales EUR14.2-15.2B at ~57% margin.
headlines.why_it_matters: CEO says customers are raising equipment demand forecasts and even expressing interest in orders for 2029 and 2030, with planned 2027-2028 supply not expected to meet demand — the first hard data point against the AI-capex-slowdown narrative that drove the chip selloff.

headlines.headline: Memory names still weak premarket: Micron -1.3%, Intel -1.1%, U.S. chip stocks down 1-2.6% in overnight trading even after ASML's raise, while Asia recovered (Samsung and SK Hynix +2%+).
headlines.why_it_matters: The CXMT 4F2 breakthrough claim remains unsubstantiated (Bloomberg's framing), so the tape is splitting: Asia is fading the scare, U.S. memory names are still repricing the supply-glut risk — single unconfirmed claim driving real price action is fragile by definition.

headlines.headline: Nvidia +0.2% premarket; reports (Bloomberg via Chip Briefing) that CEO Jensen Huang announced $2B in European deals during his tour, including a meeting with French President Macron and funding for French startups, adding to $8B invested in Europe over the past year.
headlines.why_it_matters: Sovereign-AI deal flow is the counterweight to the memory selloff for the AI complex — single-source via one outlet so far, but it puts a demand floor under the AI-capex story.

headlines.headline: Bank of America disclosed a $1.21B regulatory fine that could weigh on Q3 results; shares -1.5% premarket. Morgan Stanley +0.7% ahead of the print. BAC, MS, BlackRock, State Street all report before the open.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-outlet report so far — treat as fragile until the release — but it puts Tuesday's NII-miss fade (Citi -5.6%, WFC -3.1%) on a knife's edge: today's wave tests whether JPM's caution was company-specific or sector-wide.

headlines.headline: Tesla confirmed the postponed Roadster event will livestream Thursday Oct 15 at 7:55pm CST; Musk replied 'Timing is everything.' TSLA +0.4% overnight after dropping nearly 3% to $375.23 on Tuesday.
headlines.why_it_matters: A fresh catalyst back on the calendar nine years after the 2017 prototype reveal — hype risk is high given the delay history, but the Thursday livestream gives the tape something concrete to trade.

headlines.headline: All Magnificent Seven stocks rose premarket: Alphabet +0.7%, Meta and Amazon marginally higher, alongside futures strength.
headlines.why_it_matters: The mega-cap complex is being treated as shelter from the hardware selloff — breadth beyond software is thin, so the open hinges on whether AI names hold the bid into CPI.

usac.headline: USAC broke below its 200-day moving average ($26.92) during Monday's session, trading as low as $25.33 and last at $25.66 (reported Oct 13).
usac.why_it_matters: No fresh company news. Carried forward: TXSE listing effective Oct 5 (ticker unchanged); Oct 1 internal reorg issued 34,467,347 Class A units at $26.7206 (fixed 9.25% distribution, non-convertible, perpetual) to J-W Energy; Q2 revenue $342.1M beat vs $340.49M consensus, net income $45.7M, EPS $0.31 vs $0.28; September $600M 6.750% senior notes due 2035 to repay credit-facility borrowings; Zacks raised Q3 estimate to $0.21 EPS (Hold); consensus Hold, $29.50 average target. WTI ~$94.96 (+0.8%) is a mild sentiment backdrop for compression demand, not company news.

analysis: What changed versus the Oct 13 9 AM PT post-open brief: (1) Wednesday's CPI moved from a distant pivot to 90 minutes away — futures are pricing a calm into-the-print tape rather than a directional bet, and the 10Y's -3bp drift says the market wants a soft core print. (2) ASML resolved Bloomberg's pre-earnings question on the bullish side: the 2029/2030 order-interest comment is the strongest demand-visibility language this cycle, which is why Amsterdam is up even as U.S. ADRs read mixed overnight. (3) The memory tape is geographically splitting — Asia fading the CXMT scare (KOSPI +1.8%, Samsung/SK Hynix +2%+) while U.S. memory names keep selling off premarket — which says the unconfirmed breakthrough claim is being priced very differently by locals versus the U.S. tape. (4) Bank focus rotated from Tuesday's misses to today's wave, with the single-source BofA fine headline the one to verify at the print. Signal vs noise: CPI consensus, futures levels, ASML numbers (company PR + Dow Jones), Roadster date (company post), and bank earnings schedule are confirmed; the BofA fine size and the Nvidia $2B Europe deals rest on single outlets so far; the CXMT claim is explicitly unsubstantiated and should be treated as fragile until production evidence appears. No qualifying HN/Reddit threads — community channels were silent on these stories.
